correctness.rationale: In the energy matrix units the history equation is diagonal. Multiplying the scalar equation by t^b and differentiating gives t f''+(b+λt)f'+biωf=0, with f(0)=1 and f'(0)=−iω. Its regular Kummer solution solves the original equation by integration back from t=0. For ω≠0, Re a and Re(b−a) are positive. In Euler's integral for the Kummer solution, expand (1−x)^(b−a−1)=1+(a+1−b)x+O(x²) near x=0, with the rest exponentially suppressed because Re λ>0. Integrating against e^(−λtx)x^(a−1) gives the nonzero leading C=Γ(b)λ^(−a)/Γ(b−a) and the stated coefficient c=a(a+1−b)/λ. It is nonzero since both a and a+1−b=(λ−br)/λ are nonzero for ω≠0. Zero modes are identically one. The finite set of nonzero scalar asymptotics gives eventual invertibility; taking ratios gives a uniform expansion e^(−au)[1+c(e^(−u)−1)/t+O(t^−2)] for u in [0,U]. The diamond norm of a difference of Schur multipliers is bounded by the sum of the absolute coefficient differences, using the individual left/right coordinate projections, and the limiting multiplier equals the compound-Poisson exponential of the rate-r exponential-time averaging channel. In dimension two the exact norm is the magnitude of the off-diagonal scalar: rotation by a diagonal unitary reduces to a nonnegative factor times (Id−Ad Z)/2, and a superposition input attains it. In Hilbert–Schmidt norm the active gaps contribute in quadrature, preventing phase cancellation. The least active gap gives the slow exponent bΔ²/(r²+Δ²), strictly positive leading modulus and the claimed integrability trichotomy. No active gaps means an identically zero integrand. The finite-time normalized ratio is not assumed to be CP. Inspected RESULT.md lines 35–100, VERIFICATION.md, requirements.txt and verify.py; did not execute the frozen verifier. Its finite scalar checks do not substitute for the ancilla norm proof or the infinite-time estimate.
